purpose: Represent an actual user's scoped delegation of technical approval to a named coordinator without impersonating the user or selecting auto execution.
selection: Only an actual user instruction delegating this approval role selects this contract. Manual remains the default execution mode. An observer, ordinary task request, maintenance request or desire to avoid a blocked validator is not a delegation. Read docs/scoped-approval.md completely before adoption.
authority: The actual conversation supplies authority; a local record does not create or authenticate it. registerScopedMandate records the exact reviewed manual Plan, designated coordinator, executing task, Work/repository realpaths, every job's local/isolated technical ceiling and terminal boundary. The user's grant can precede future goal presentations; record the coordinator's later concrete decision as actor assistant, never as a fabricated user reply.
provenance: Preserve actual actor, source thread and exact quote. Use a real native messageId only when exposed. Otherwise use messageId null, messageIdAvailability not-exposed and assurance conversation-context-not-authenticated. A local record ID, turn ID, requestId or digest must never masquerade as a native message ID. These records are auditable contextual assertions, not cryptographic signatures.
sequence: Present each bounded goal briefly in its actual task with links to the complete goal. presentDelegatedGoal binds that real presentation. authorizeDelegatedGoal records a designated coordinator decision and grounded low/medium reversible risk assessment. requestCell requires explicit coordinator/task identities and a fresh context-bound assessment for that stage. Typed outputs, current Work dependencies, exact resource effects, unchanged producer artifacts and existing implementation source anchors still gate execution. acceptDelegatedDelivery separately reviews the current complete result. markWorkDone and completion preflight remain mandatory.
technicalQuestions: An optional per-job mandate ceiling technicalQuestions lists unique exact job.openQuestions strings explicitly reviewed as technical within the user's delegated scope. Omission, including historical mandates, defaults to no question-answering authority. Freeze this classification with the mandate and actual review provenance, not unknown future answers. Before each goal presentation, freeze exactly one nonempty {question, answer} pair per job question in goal.inputs.planQuestionAnswers; every question must be allowlisted for that exact job. The actual coordinator decision binds these answers. Changed answers require a fresh goal presentation/decision; changed Plan or mandate classification cannot reuse old receipts. Plan-wide questions and unlisted/business choices stay blocked. Exact matching cannot authenticate a classification or make expanded effects permissible; all existing scope and risk gates remain mandatory. This does not change direct manual or auto authority.
limits: No auto budget, global setting, scheduler or third execution mode is introduced. No unresolved product choices, reserved publication/deployment/real-data effects, migration, runtime self-update or bootstrap edits inherit this mandate. Unknown/high risk, changed scope/stage context, revoked/terminal state or stale proof stops before new effects. A goal or Plan revision needs a fresh actual coordinator review within still-valid user authority, not mutation of old receipts.
persistence: Mandate state lives under the bound Work root's excluded _local/approvals directory; every new effect rereads it. Preserve the original immutable mandate and truthful revoked/completed status. Run state stays in the same four-file Plan bundle. loadPlanRuns preserves presentation provenance. saveDelegatedCompletion verifies all current accepted producers and terminal criteria before marking the Plan done and closing the mandate.
review: These checks validate consistency, not whether a quote was truly said or an environment is genuinely isolated. The coordinator must inspect actual intent, targets, isolation and output. Never call a technical UAT acceptance human UAT merely because the coordinator accepted its proof. Direct manual user approval and explicit auto approval retain their separate strict contracts.
